Package org.aeonbits.owner

Class TemplateTool

java.lang.Object
org.aeonbits.owner.TemplateTool
public final class TemplateTool extends Object
Writes the properties file of a mapping interface, from the command line, without running the application it belongs to. 
     java -cp app.jar:owner.jar org.aeonbits.owner.TemplateTool com.acme.MyConfig
     java -cp app.jar:owner.jar org.aeonbits.owner.TemplateTool --into src/main/resources com.acme.MyConfig com.acme.Other

This is the other half of #3, open since 2013. The half that needed designing is Accessible.save(File), which writes the file keeping the one that is already there - its order, its blank lines, and every comment except the ones the interface owns. This tool is that same writer with a main in front of it, and it exists for a reason worth stating: save is declared on Accessible, so a configuration that does not extend it - which is most of them, and certainly every one that has no file yet - could not generate anything at all.

Only the Config.DefaultValue of each method is written. No source is read, and that is deliberate: a template is what the code says the configuration is, and a tool that loaded the sources would put the machine it ran on into the file - the environment, a password from a home directory, the host name of somebody's laptop.

With --into the file goes where the convention looks for it, <dir>/com/acme/MyConfig.properties, so a directory that is a resources root produces a configuration the library finds with no @Sources at all. Without it, the template goes to standard output and can be redirected - but for one interface only, two of them being two files and not one.

Run it twice and the second run keeps what you edited in between: it is the same writer, so a value you changed by hand stays changed, a key you added stays where you put it, and the descriptions come back from the code.
